choice_d: In a separate paragraph titled "Agency Disclosure" within the brokerage services agreement, or in a separate writing titled "Agency Disclosure" signed by the principal
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.87(i) requires the agency-type disclosure, along with disclosure of compensation terms offered to another brokerage firm representing a different party, to be set forth in a separate paragraph titled "Agency Disclosure" in the brokerage services agreement, or in a separate writing titled "Agency Disclosure" signed by the principal, no later than when the principal signs the brokerage services agreement.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.87(i), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.2 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.87(d), what must a brokerage firm generally do with every written offer or counteroffer it receives, regardless of whether the property is already under an existing contract?
choice_a: Present it in a timely manner and provide written confirmation of receipt to the other party or its agent or transaction broker, unless the principal has directed otherwise in writing
choice_b: Discard any offer received after the first accepted offer without informing anyone
choice_c: Present only offers that meet or exceed the list price
choice_d: Wait until the existing contract falls through before acknowledging any other offer
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.87(d) imposes a non-waivable (absent written direction from the principal) duty to present all written offers and counteroffers in a timely manner and to provide written confirmation of receipt to the other party or its agent or transaction broker, regardless of whether the property is already subject to an existing contract for sale.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.87(d), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.2 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(a), a brokerage firm that performs real estate brokerage services for a buyer is presumed to be which type of agent by default?
choice_a: A seller's agent, regardless of who the firm is actually working with
choice_b: A buyer's agent, unless a specific statutory exception applies (such as the firm already representing the seller, having agreed to act as a transaction broker, or the broker/salesperson being the seller)
choice_c: A transaction broker, unless the buyer objects in writing
choice_d: No agency relationship exists unless a court later determines one
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(a) establishes that a brokerage firm performing brokerage services for a buyer is a buyer's agent by default, unless one of the enumerated exceptions applies, such as the firm already representing the seller under a brokerage services agreement.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(a), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.3 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(b), which disclosure must a brokerage services agreement between a brokerage firm and a buyer expressly include?
choice_a: A statement that the buyer's agent's commission rate is fixed by the New Jersey Real Estate Commission
choice_b: A guarantee that the buyer will close within 60 days
choice_c: A statement expressly stating that broker compensation is fully negotiable and not set by law
choice_d: A waiver of the buyer's right to review the agreement with an attorney
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(b)(2)(g) requires a brokerage services agreement with a buyer to include a disclosure expressly stating that broker compensation is fully negotiable and not set by law.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(b)(2)(g), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.3 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(b)(1), is a written brokerage services agreement required between a brokerage firm and a buyer in a commercial real estate transaction?
choice_a: Yes — it is required in every transaction, residential or commercial, with no exceptions
choice_b: No — brokerage services agreements are never required with buyers under any circumstances
choice_c: Yes, but only if the buyer is a first-time purchaser
choice_d: No — a brokerage services agreement is required with a buyer in a residential transaction, but is not required between a brokerage firm and a buyer in a commercial real estate transaction
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(b)(1) requires a brokerage firm to enter into a brokerage services agreement with a buyer in a residential real estate transaction, but expressly states that such an agreement shall not be required between a brokerage firm and a buyer in a commercial real estate transaction.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.88(b)(1), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.3 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.89(b), does a buyer's agent breach its duty of loyalty by showing a property in which its buyer client is interested to other prospective buyers?
choice_a: No — showing that property to other prospective buyers does not breach the duty of loyalty to the buyer or create a conflict of interest
choice_b: Yes — showing the property to any other buyer automatically terminates the agency relationship
choice_c: Yes — this is treated as an undisclosed dual agency violation
choice_d: No, but only if the agent charges the other prospective buyers a separate fee
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.89(b)(1) expressly provides that the showing of a property in which a buyer is interested to other prospective buyers by a buyer's agent does not breach the duty of loyalty to that buyer or create a conflict of interest.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.89(b)(1), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.4 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.91(b), may a seller's agent show properties not owned by their seller client to prospective buyers, or list competing properties for sale, without breaching a duty to that seller?
choice_a: No — a seller's agent may never show or list any other property while representing a seller
choice_b: Yes — showing properties not owned by the seller to prospective buyers, or listing competing properties, does not breach the duty of loyalty to the seller or create a conflict of interest
choice_c: Yes, but only with the seller's advance written waiver of the conflict
choice_d: No — doing so automatically converts the agent into a disclosed dual agent
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.91(b)(1) provides that a seller's agent showing properties not owned by the seller to prospective buyers, or listing competing properties for sale, does not breach the duty of loyalty to the seller or create a conflict of interest.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.91(b)(1), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.6 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.92(c), may a broker acting as a disclosed dual agent in a transaction be compensated by both the buyer and the seller through the brokerage firm?
choice_a: No — a disclosed dual agent may only ever be compensated by the seller
choice_b: No — receiving compensation from both parties is automatically fraud regardless of disclosure
choice_c: Yes — notwithstanding other provisions of the license law, a disclosed dual agent may receive compensation through the brokerage firm from either or both parties, provided the sources and amounts of compensation are disclosed in writing to the buyer and seller
choice_d: Yes, but only if the compensation from each party is identical in amount
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.92(c) provides that, notwithstanding chapter 15 of Title 45 or any other law to the contrary (including R.S.45:15-17), a broker, broker-salesperson, or salesperson acting as a disclosed dual agent may receive compensation through the brokerage firm from either or both the buyer and seller, provided the sources and amounts of compensation are disclosed in writing to both.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.92(c), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.7 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.93(a)(1), are a seller's designated agent and a buyer's designated agent, from the same brokerage firm, considered dual agents?
choice_a: Yes — every designated agent arrangement is legally identical to a disclosed dual agency
choice_b: No — designated agents owe no fiduciary duty to anyone
choice_c: Yes, but only if they work out of the same branch office
choice_d: No — designated agents are not dual agents and each owes fiduciary duties solely to their own respective principal
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.93(a)(1) specifies that, for purposes of designated agency, the seller's designated agent and the buyer's designated agent are not dual agents and owe fiduciary duties solely to their respective principals.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.93(a)(1), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.8 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.93(a)(2), what must occur for a designated agency relationship to take effect in a residential real estate transaction?
choice_a: The brokerage firm must enter into a written designated agency agreement (which may be incorporated into the brokerage services agreement) with each party, including the informed, written consent of each party
choice_b: Nothing further — designated agency automatically arises whenever two different salespersons from the same firm are involved
choice_c: Only the broker of record's internal notes are required, with no consent from either party
choice_d: A designated agency relationship can only be created by a court order
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.93(a)(2) requires the brokerage firm to enter into a written designated agency agreement with each party, which may be incorporated into the brokerage services agreement in a residential transaction, and which must include the informed, written consent of each party to the transaction.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.93(a)(2), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.8 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.94(a), what is a transaction broker prohibited from doing that would otherwise be expected of an agent?
choice_a: A transaction broker is prohibited from ever communicating with the buyer directly
choice_b: A transaction broker shall not act as an agent for or represent any party, shall not promote one party's interest over the other, and is not required to keep any information confidential
choice_c: A transaction broker is prohibited from collecting any compensation under any circumstances
choice_d: A transaction broker is prohibited from managing the closing process
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.94(a) specifies that a brokerage firm engaged as a transaction broker shall not act as an agent for, or represent, any party, shall not promote the interest of one party over the other, and shall not be required to keep any information confidential — distinguishing the role from that of an agent.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.94(a), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.9 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(b), when is written confirmation of termination required for an agency or transaction broker relationship to end?
choice_a: Written confirmation is always required, no matter how the relationship ends
choice_b: Written confirmation is never required under any circumstances
choice_c: Written confirmation is required when the relationship is terminated by mutual agreement or by written notice from either party, but is not required when the relationship ends through completion of performance or expiration of its agreed term
choice_d: Written confirmation is required only if the property has not yet sold
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(b) requires written confirmation of termination when a relationship ends by mutual agreement or by written notice under the brokerage services agreement, but does not require written confirmation when the relationship instead ends through completion of performance or expiration of the agreed term.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(a)-(b), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.10 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(c), what duties does a brokerage firm generally continue to owe after an agency or transaction broker relationship has terminated?
choice_a: None whatsoever — all duties end immediately and completely upon termination
choice_b: The full range of fiduciary duties owed during the relationship, unchanged, indefinitely
choice_c: Only the duty to continue marketing the property at no additional cost
choice_d: Only the duty to provide a timely accounting for money and property received on behalf of any party, and to not disclose confidential information from an agency relationship
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(c) provides that, except as otherwise agreed in writing, a brokerage firm owes no further duty after termination other than to provide a timely accounting for money and property received on behalf of any party, and to not disclose confidential information if there was an agency relationship.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(c), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.10 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(d), absent termination by expiration or a completed closing, how must a disclosed dual agent's brokerage services agreement with a buyer or seller be terminated?
choice_a: In writing, signed by the buyer or seller as applicable, with confirmed delivery to the disclosed dual agent
choice_b: By a simple verbal statement made to any employee of the brokerage firm
choice_c: It cannot be terminated early under any circumstances once dual agency consent is given
choice_d: By posting a notice on the property's exterior
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(d) requires that, absent termination by expiration or fulfillment through a completed closing, a disclosed dual agent's brokerage services agreements with the buyer and seller be terminated only in writing, signed by the applicable party, with confirmed delivery to the disclosed dual agent.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.95(d), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.10 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.96(b), does an agreement to pay, or the actual payment of, brokerage compensation by itself create an agency relationship between the payor and the brokerage firm?
choice_a: Yes — paying any compensation automatically makes the payor a represented client
choice_b: No — an agreement to pay or payment of compensation shall not establish an agency relationship between the party who paid the compensation and the brokerage firm
choice_c: Yes, but only if the payor is the buyer rather than the seller
choice_d: No, but only for commercial transactions
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.96(b) makes clear that an agreement to pay or the payment of compensation does not, by itself, establish an agency relationship between the paying party and the brokerage firm — compensation source and representation are legally distinct.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.96(b), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.11 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.96(e), may a brokerage firm be compensated by more than one party to the same real estate transaction?
choice_a: No — accepting compensation from more than one party is always an absolute violation with no exceptions
choice_b: Yes, but only if the brokerage firm is acting solely as a transaction broker
choice_c: Yes — notwithstanding chapter 15 of Title 45 or any other contrary law, a brokerage firm may be compensated by more than one party regardless of the agency or transaction broker relationship it has with the parties
choice_d: No — only the New Jersey Real Estate Commission itself may authorize dual compensation on a case-by-case basis
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.96(e) provides that, notwithstanding chapter 15 of Title 45 or any other law, rule, or regulation to the contrary (including R.S.45:15-17), a brokerage firm may be compensated by more than one party for real estate brokerage services regardless of the agency or transaction broker relationship it has with the parties.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.96(e), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.11 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.97(a), when may a principal (buyer or seller) be held liable for an act, error, or omission by their agent or transaction broker?
choice_a: A principal is automatically and fully liable for every act of their agent with no limitation
choice_b: A principal can never be held liable for an agent's conduct under any circumstances
choice_c: A principal is liable only if the agent was compensated on a flat-fee basis
choice_d: Generally, only if the principal participated in or authorized the act, error, or omission, or to the extent the principal benefited from it (in which case liability is limited to the amount of that benefit, absent punitive damages)
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.97(a) generally shields a principal from liability for an agent's or transaction broker's act, error, or omission unless the principal participated in or authorized it, or except to the extent the principal benefited, in which case liability is capped at the monetary benefit absent an award of punitive damages.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.97(a), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.12 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.98, if a brokerage firm knows a material fact about a transaction that its principal does not actually know, is the principal automatically charged with that knowledge?
choice_a: No — unless otherwise agreed to in writing, a principal may not be charged with knowledge or notice of facts known by the brokerage firm that are not actually known by the principal
choice_b: Yes — a principal is always legally deemed to know everything their brokerage firm knows
choice_c: No — but only if the principal is a first-time buyer or seller
choice_d: Yes, but only for commercial transactions
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.98 provides that, unless otherwise agreed to in writing, a principal may not be charged with knowledge or notice of facts known by the brokerage firm representing or working with the principal that are not actually known by the principal, and the reverse also applies to the brokerage firm.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.98, enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.13 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.99(a), what must be posted at a residential property showing that is generally open to the public (such as an open house), where the hosting brokerage firm represents only the seller?
choice_a: Nothing — no posted notice of any kind is required at open houses in New Jersey
choice_b: A sign at the entrance or a sign-in sheet clearly advising prospective buyers that the hosting brokerage firm represents the seller only and has no relationship with the prospective buyer, subject to a limited statutory exception
choice_c: Only the asking price, with no mention of representation
choice_d: A sign is required only if more than 20 people attend the open house
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.99(a) requires that at any residential property showing generally open to the public, a sign be posted at the entrance or a sign-in sheet clearly advise prospective buyers that the hosting brokerage firm represents the seller only and has no relationship with the prospective buyer, except where the buyer is unrepresented and agrees to the seller's agent becoming a disclosed dual or designated agent.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.99(a), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.14 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under the statutory open-house sign text set out in N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.99(b), what is a buyer who already has exclusive representation by a buyer's agent required to do?
choice_a: Immediately leave the open house without signing in
choice_b: Nothing — existing representation need never be disclosed at an open house
choice_c: Disclose that existing exclusive buyer-agent representation on the sign-in sheet
choice_d: Pay a disclosure fee to the hosting brokerage firm
explanation: The statutorily prescribed open-house sign text in N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.99(b) states that if the buyer is already exclusively represented by a buyer's agent, the buyer is required to disclose this representation on the sign-in sheet.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16.99(b), enacted by P.L.2024, c.32, s.14 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-12, what must every New Jersey real estate broker maintain, and what must be prominently displayed there?
choice_a: A private, invitation-only office that the public may not enter under any circumstances
choice_b: No physical office at all, provided the broker has a working phone number
choice_c: A main office, but display of license certificates is discretionary
choice_d: A designated main office open to the public, with the license certificate of the broker and all licensed persons in the broker's employ prominently displayed
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 requires every real estate broker to maintain a designated main office open to the public, with the license certificate of the broker and of all licensed persons in the broker's employ prominently displayed there.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-12, what must be conspicuously displayed on the exterior of every place of business maintained by a New Jersey real estate broker?
choice_a: The name in which the broker is authorized to operate (and, for a corporation or partnership, the name of the individual licensed as its authorized broker) along with the words "Licensed Real Estate Broker"
choice_b: Only the broker's personal cell phone number, in letters at least six inches tall
choice_c: A list of every property currently listed by the office
choice_d: Nothing is required on the exterior of a broker's office under New Jersey law
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 requires that every place of business maintained by a real estate broker have conspicuously displayed on its exterior the name under which the broker is authorized to operate (and, for a corporation or partnership, the name of the individual licensed as its authorized broker), together with the words "Licensed Real Estate Broker."
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-12, if a New Jersey real estate broker maintains more than one place of business, what is required for each additional (branch) office?
choice_a: No separate license is needed as long as the branch shares the same street name as the main office
choice_b: A separate branch office license must be issued for each branch office, and the branch office must be under the direct supervision of a broker-salesperson
choice_c: Branch offices are prohibited outright under New Jersey law
choice_d: A branch office may be supervised remotely by a licensee in another state
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 requires that a broker maintaining more than one place of business obtain a separate branch office license for each branch office, and that each branch office be under the direct supervision of a broker-salesperson.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-12, what obligation applies to a real estate broker whose main office is located in another state?
choice_a: No out-of-state licensing obligation applies as long as the broker only transacts business by phone
choice_b: The broker must relocate the main office to New Jersey within 90 days
choice_c: The broker must maintain a valid real estate broker's license in good standing in the state where that office is located
choice_d: The broker is automatically exempt from all New Jersey licensing requirements
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 requires a real estate broker whose main office is located in another state to maintain a valid real estate broker's license in good standing in the state where that office is located.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-12 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-13, what happens if a licensed New Jersey broker changes business addresses without giving written notice to the New Jersey Real Estate Commission and without a new broker's license being issued?
choice_a: Nothing happens as long as mail is eventually forwarded to the new address
choice_b: The broker is simply issued a warning letter with no effect on the license
choice_c: The change is presumed valid after 6 months even without notice
choice_d: The license previously issued is automatically canceled
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-13 provides that a change of business address without notification to the commission, and without the issuance of a new broker's license, automatically cancels the license previously issued.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-13 (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(c) identifies which advertising-related conduct as a specific ground for license discipline?
choice_a: Pursuing a flagrant and continued course of misrepresentation or making false promises through agents, broker-salespersons, salespersons, advertisements, or otherwise
choice_b: Using professional real estate photography in a listing advertisement
choice_c: Advertising the accurate square footage of a home as listed in public tax records
choice_d: Including the broker's license number in a print advertisement
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(c) makes it a disciplinable offense to pursue a flagrant and continued course of misrepresentation, or the making of false promises, through agents, broker-salespersons, salespersons, advertisements, or otherwise.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(c) (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(g), which promotional practice for the sale of real estate is specifically identified as a ground for license discipline?
choice_a: Offering a free market analysis to a prospective seller
choice_b: Using a plan, scheme, or method for the sale or promotion of real estate that involves a lottery, contest, game, prize, drawing, or offering a lot or parcel for advertising purposes
choice_c: Hosting a traditional open house with light refreshments
choice_d: Advertising a property using a virtual 3D walkthrough tour
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(g) makes it a disciplinable offense to use any plan, scheme, or method for the sale or promotion of the sale of real estate that involves a lottery, a contest, a game, a prize, a drawing, or the offering of a lot or parcel for advertising purposes.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(g) (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(j), what advertising or representational conduct involving a real estate organization is specifically identified as a ground for license discipline?
choice_a: Displaying a valid, current membership insignia of an organization the licensee actually belongs to
choice_b: Listing the licensee's own name on a business card
choice_c: Using any trade name or insignia of membership in a real estate organization of which the licensee is not actually a member
choice_d: Referencing the local multiple listing service by its correct legal name
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(j) makes it a disciplinable offense to use any trade name or insignia of membership in a real estate organization of which the licensee is not actually a member — for example, falsely implying Realtor® designation or association membership the licensee doesn't hold.
source_note: N.J.S.A. 45:15-17(j) (live-verified via law.justia.com, 2025 N.J. Rev. Stat.)

topic: NJ Agency Disclosure, Advertising, Listings & Place of Business
question: Under N.J.S.A. 45:15-16b, when a New Jersey broker advertises a lawful purchaser rebate, what must the advertisement include, and how must it be displayed?
choice_a: Nothing further is required beyond stating the rebate amount
choice_b: A disclaimer written in text smaller than a standard footnote is sufficient
choice_c: Only a disclosure of the broker's license number, with no tax-related language required
choice_d: A disclosure about the purchaser's obligation to pay any applicable taxes on the rebate and a notice to contact a tax professional, both clearly and conspicuously displayed in text at least as large as the advertisement's own text
explanation: N.J.S.A. 45:15-16b requires that any advertisement for a lawful purchaser rebate include a disclosure about the purchaser's obligation to pay applicable taxes and a notice to consult a tax professional, with both clearly and conspicuously displayed in text equal to or larger than the size of the text used for the advertisement itself.
